root_cause.text: In the pf1550 charger driver probe path, `devm_request_threaded_irq()` was called before `devm_power_supply_register()`, so devres teardown order allowed the IRQ handler to run after the `power_supply` object was freed or before it was initialized, causing `power_supply_changed()` to use an invalid `power_supply` handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the IRQ request loop from before to after the `devm_power_supply_register()` calls, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that requesting the IRQ first causes reverse-order `devm_` cleanup to free/unregister the `power_supply` before unregistering the IRQ, creating a removal race and also allowing interrupts during probe before the `power_supply` handle is registered.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove charger IRQ acquisition and registration from pf1550_charger_probe() so probe no longer sets up interrupts in this path.
intent_record.what: The patch removes the entire for-loop in pf1550_charger_probe() that iterated over PF1550_CHARGER_IRQ_NR, fetched each IRQ with platform_get_irq(), stored it in chg->virqs[i], and registered each interrupt with devm_request_threaded_irq() using pf1550_charger_irq_handler.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe function no longer retrieves or requests charger IRQs during device initialization, so this driver instance will not register its interrupt handler from this code path and will no longer fail probe due to missing IRQs or IRQ request errors here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register all PF1550 charger IRQs during probe so charger interrupts are handled correctly and probe fails if IRQ setup cannot be completed.
intent_record.what: A new loop was added in pf1550_charger_probe() that iterates from 0 to PF1550_CHARGER_IRQ_NR - 1, retrieves each platform IRQ with platform_get_irq(), stores it in chg->virqs[i], and registers a threaded interrupt handler with devm_request_threaded_irq() using pf1550_charger_irq_handler and IRQF_NO_SUSPEND; the function now returns immediately on IRQ retrieval or registration failure.
intent_record.how: At probe time, the charger driver now acquires and registers all defined charger IRQs so interrupt events can be handled at runtime, including during suspend due to IRQF_NO_SUSPEND. It also stops initialization if any required IRQ is missing or cannot be requested, preventing the device from running without its interrupt handling set up.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is IRQ setup in pf1550_charger_probe() occurring in the wrong order relative to power_supply registration. Removing charger IRQ acquisition/registration from that probe path directly eliminates the problematic IRQ lifecycle and handler invocation there.

The change directly concerns when and how PF1550 charger IRQs are registered during probe, which is the same area as the root cause: IRQ registration order relative to power_supply registration. Since the bug is caused by requesting IRQs too early in probe, changes to probe-time IRQ setup are directly related.

candidates.rationale: This is the key ordering bug: IRQ devres is acquired in probe before the power_supply is registered, so teardown happens in reverse order and the IRQ can remain active after the power_supply object is freed, or fire before it is initialized.

This registration happens only after IRQ setup in the pre-fix probe flow, establishing the unsafe lifetime ordering that allows the IRQ handler to call power_supply_changed() on an invalid or uninitialized handle.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement requests and registers the IRQ before the power_supply object is created. Because devres releases resources in reverse order, this earlier IRQ registration causes teardown to free the power_supply before the IRQ is disabled/freed, allowing the handler to run with an invalid or not-yet-initialized power_supply handle.

bic_trace_step.reason: The probe function clearly shows the problematic ordering. In `pf1550_charger_probe()`, the loop requests IRQs first via `devm_request_threaded_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, NULL, pf1550_charger_irq_handler, IRQF_NO_SUSPEND, "pf1550-charger", chg);` before either power supply is registered. Only afterward does the code call `chg->charger = devm_power_supply_register(...)` and `chg->battery = devm_power_supply_register(...)`. This matches the root cause: devres will release resources in reverse order, so on teardown the power supplies can be freed before the IRQs are released, allowing the IRQ handler/work path to access invalid `power_supply` pointers. The IRQ path is relevant because `pf1550_charger_irq_handler()` schedules delayed work, and `pf1550_chg_vbus_work()` calls `power_supply_changed(chg->battery);` and `power_supply_changed(chg->charger);`. Since those handles are assigned only after IRQ registration, interrupts can also occur before initialization. There is no protective check preventing use before registration or after teardown, and no reordered registration that would constitute the fix.
